These computed keys resolve to literal strings (both normally `[object Object]`), and Zod objects strip unknown properties by default. Consequently, a sync response containing `access_token`, `expires_in`, and `refresh_token` loses the expiry and refresh token during parsing. Zoom then computes an invalid expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the returned expiry. Define explicit supported fields or use an appropriate catchall/passthrough schema."
    },

      "title": "Google refresh persists the parse-result wrapper instead of credentials",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a safeParse result shaped as `{ success: true, data: ... }`, unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call, which returned the credential object itself. Saving that result directly as `Credential.key` removes the access token and other required fields from the top level. After the first successful refresh, subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse the saved credentials. This also affects installations with credential syncing disabled; persist the parsed `.data` instead."
    },

      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Sync refresh returns a Fetch Response to callers expecting SDK results",
      "body": "The sync branch returns an unparsed Fetch `Response`, while several callers expect the return shape of their original refresh function. Google reads `res.data`, Zoho CRM and Bigin read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads `accessToken` and `expiresIn` directly. None of those properties exist on a Fetch Response. Enabling syncing therefore causes those integrations to throw or use undefined tokens even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize the sync response and adapt each caller to a defined return contract."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy token",
      "body": "This fallback runs even when credential syncing is disabled. Office 365's response schema explicitly allows an omitted `refresh_token`; previously its merge preserved the existing usable refresh token in that case. The helper now inserts the literal `refresh_token`, which overwrites the stored token during the merge. The next refresh sends that dummy value to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement."
    },

This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without checking, throws a ReferenceError after the token request succeeds. Import the Prisma client so Salesforce client initialization can complete."
    },

      "line": 75,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "Salesforce unconditionally refreshes directly against Salesforce instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`. When syncing is enabled, its parser nevertheless switches to the shared-response schema. Thus Salesforce never asks the configured parent application for refreshed credentials and continues independently refreshing its tokens, contrary to the source-of-truth behavior implemented for the other integrations. Apply the same endpoint routing here before selecting the shared-response parser."
    },
    {

      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not the credential ID",
      "body": "The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID and is sent to the parent application as `calcomUserId`. This caller passes `credentialId`, which identifies a credential row instead. Those IDs are independent, so the endpoint either cannot find the owner or returns tokens for a different user whose user ID happens to match. Carry `credential.userId` into this method and pass that value."
    },

      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Use the actual Zoom app slug in sync requests",
      "body": "The refresh request sends `appSlug: \"zoomvideo\"`, but Zoom credentials are installed with `appId: \"zoom\"` and the webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent store using that same slug contract cannot match this refresh to the Zoom credentials it synced. Pass `\"zoom\"` rather than the integration directory name."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make first-time credential synchronization atomic",
      "body": "The existence check and credential creation are separate operations, and user/app credentials are not unique. Two concurrent deliveries for a user's first sync can both find no credential and both create one. Future deliveries update only the arbitrary row returned by `findFirst`, leaving another credential stale and available to integration consumers. Serialize this operation or introduce an appropriate unique identity and atomic upsert so concurrent webhook deliveries cannot create duplicates."
    }

findings.title: The minimum response schema strips expiry and refresh-token fields
findings.body: Using a Zod schema's `.toString()` as an object key does not define a wildcard property. These computed keys resolve to literal strings (both normally `[object Object]`), and Zod objects strip unknown properties by default. Consequently, a sync response containing `access_token`, `expires_in`, and `refresh_token` loses the expiry and refresh token during parsing. Zoom then computes an invalid expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the returned expiry. Define explicit supported fields or use an appropriate catchall/passthrough schema.

findings.title: Google refresh persists the parse-result wrapper instead of credentials
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a safeParse result shaped as `{ success: true, data: ... }`, unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call, which returned the credential object itself. Saving that result directly as `Credential.key` removes the access token and other required fields from the top level. After the first successful refresh, subsequent GoogleCalendarService instances cannot parse the saved credentials. This also affects installations with credential syncing disabled; persist the parsed `.data` instead.

findings.title: Sync refresh returns a Fetch Response to callers expecting SDK results
findings.body: The sync branch returns an unparsed Fetch `Response`, while several callers expect the return shape of their original refresh function. Google reads `res.data`, Zoho CRM and Bigin read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads `accessToken` and `expiresIn` directly. None of those properties exist on a Fetch Response. Enabling syncing therefore causes those integrations to throw or use undefined tokens even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Normalize the sync response and adapt each caller to a defined return contract.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a dummy token
findings.body: This fallback runs even when credential syncing is disabled. Office 365's response schema explicitly allows an omitted `refresh_token`; previously its merge preserved the existing usable refresh token in that case. The helper now inserts the literal `refresh_token`, which overwrites the stored token during the merge. The next refresh sends that dummy value to Microsoft and fails. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not return a replacement.

findings.title: Import Prisma before updating Salesforce credentials
findings.body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file does not import or declare `prisma`. This fails TypeScript checking and, if executed without checking, throws a ReferenceError after the token request succeeds. Import the Prisma client so Salesforce client initialization can complete.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: Salesforce unconditionally refreshes directly against Salesforce instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`. When syncing is enabled, its parser nevertheless switches to the shared-response schema. Thus Salesforce never asks the configured parent application for refreshed credentials and continues independently refreshing its tokens, contrary to the source-of-truth behavior implemented for the other integrations. Apply the same endpoint routing here before selecting the shared-response parser.

findings.title: Pass the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not the credential ID
findings.body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID and is sent to the parent application as `calcomUserId`. This caller passes `credentialId`, which identifies a credential row instead. Those IDs are independent, so the endpoint either cannot find the owner or returns tokens for a different user whose user ID happens to match. Carry `credential.userId` into this method and pass that value.

findings.title: Use the actual Zoom app slug in sync requests
findings.body: The refresh request sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`, but Zoom credentials are installed with `appId: "zoom"` and the webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent store using that same slug contract cannot match this refresh to the Zoom credentials it synced. Pass `"zoom"` rather than the integration directory name.

findings.title: Make first-time credential synchronization atomic
findings.body: The existence check and credential creation are separate operations, and user/app credentials are not unique. Two concurrent deliveries for a user's first sync can both find no credential and both create one. Future deliveries update only the arbitrary row returned by `findFirst`, leaving another credential stale and available to integration consumers. Serialize this operation or introduce an appropriate unique identity and atomic upsert so concurrent webhook deliveries cannot create duplicates.
